scores.one_line: Novelty is a vocabulary artifact: the feasible variant collapses to Calinon/Kendall-Gal variance weighting, the novel variant needs counterfactual rollout supervision that does not exist, and the robustness causal chain to perception-driven LIBERO-Plus failures never closes.

Treats a systematic domain shift as sensor corruption; with n=2 complementary cameras Dempster-Shafer degenerates to a scalar gate, the wrist-cam fallback lacks scene geometry, and the mandatory corruption-augmentation baseline is a strict superset of its own training signal.

Observable error signal and lab-evidenced probes (R^2=0.75) are real assets, but the mechanism is internally incoherent on its headline factor (referent Delta is identically zero under robot-init shift) and double-counts against a partially-perceiving closed-loop expert.

Identifiability contradiction at the core: clean LIBERO data has constant camera/light metadata so the nuisance subspace is unlearnable without re-rendering, and any rescue collapses the by-construction edge over augmentation while the held-out factors (occlusion, viewpoint) sit outside a low-rank linear repair's reach.

Episode-constant amortized nuisance inference is a genuinely distinct TTA combination with every causal link measurable, but the gate-flagged span gap (a basis fit on appearance-invariant clean features has no reason to contain test-time viewpoint displacements) makes the premise more likely false than true.

The cheapest, most falsifiable proposal in the batch (2 GPU-h kill test, zero params) but seed noise driving a 23-46pt long-horizon gap is mechanistically implausible, and the direction-split lives inside the crowded ACT/VOTE/BoN cluster; its main value is the stochasticity decomposition even on a kill.

Mechanistically the soundest survivor: retry arithmetic p->p(2-p) attacks the multiplicative failure structure directly, the physical-state reset answers the monitor-cluster kills, and the diagnostic is free on existing logs — but verify-then-retry is classical robotics, so it publishes as an honest measurement-plus-fix paper, not a new mechanism.

The monotone-in-time signature is an elegant falsifiable prediction, but it inherits S1's unlearnable nuisance projector, its three axes are largely one measurement re-sliced, and the photometric slice it scopes to is the mildest LIBERO-Plus factor.

Well-posed closed-form machinery with a cheap offline falsification and a genuine abstention axis on the uncharacterized few-shot bottleneck, but every component maps to known GP/selective-prediction work and the headline concedes LoRA may win nominal SR.

Compounds S1's broken identifiability with S3's conceded novelty into a two-stage system with multiplied premise risk; the own fallback plan to split into two papers concedes it is not one contribution.

Audit-clean novelty target (single-observation attractor repair vs the memory-for-long-horizon cluster) but attractor completion cannot invert a high-rank viewpoint warp, prototype snapping risks harming novel-object content, and it affirmatively moves only 1-2 axes.

Reliability-arbitrated dual control is already implemented on robots three times over (audit 0.4, batch floor), and a proprioception-only habit branch cannot carry manipulation subtasks alone, capping the robustness recovery it promises.

IB-for-invariance has real supporting evidence (DRIBO, VDB) so some photometric robustness gain is credible, but it is a benchmark/backbone transfer of a 2017-2020 technique and the agentview/wrist pair are complementary views whose shared information may strip task content.

Clean transplant with a fatal gate-C flaw: the action-execution error it filters is unobservable at deployment (proprio tracking error is near zero for a wrongly-targeted command), so the mechanism-to-metric chain breaks at its first link and a 10-parameter EMA-with-branding remains.

The one candidate with a genuine latency mechanism (skip backbone calls inside the funnel), trivially cheap to build, but VLA-Corrector already ships the identical event-triggered pattern (audit 0.25) and the prescribed-performance guarantee is hollow for a monitor-only wrapper.

A proven zero-NFE-cost diffusion trick with plausible modest sample-quality gains, but it is a zero-adaptation transplant of Analog Bits and its long-horizon premise (per-chunk sampling noise drives the 23-46pt gap) is the same unevidenced link that sank R3.

Projector's training signal needs counterfactual sim rollouts that don't exist, and every ablation is a full action-expert retrain per seed on one shared A100 - weeks of GPU for a loss-weighting delta a heteroscedastic baseline likely matches.

Small MLP heads are easy, but the required corruption generator IS the confound: the augmentation-only baseline uses the same machinery and probably eats the gain, and DS fusion of 2 cameras is just a scalar gate.

Inference wrapper with existing HDF5 labels is buildable, but it's a pile of hand-tuned parts (ramp, referent switch, ILC buffer) with classic EE-frame bugs and slice-tuned-constants confound risk; reviewer2 showed the referent Delta is zero on its headline init-state factor.

Unbuildable as specced: clean LIBERO has constant camera/light so the nuisance probes have no label variance - the engineer discovers mid-build that a re-render pipeline is mandatory, which collapses the whole anti-augmentation pitch.

Cleanest integration in the batch (one connector-output hook, PCA basis, closed-form fit, cheap decisive diagnostic), but gate C's span gap is real - a clean-data basis has no reason to contain the viewpoint displacement, so expect the diagnostic to kill it cheaply.

Two days of engineering, zero params, runs on the in-house LIBERO-Long harness with a 2-GPU-hour kill test - the easiest build here, but crowded BoN/ensembling territory and the seed-noise premise is unevidenced, so it's cheap lab knowledge more than a paper.

Most engineer-credible SR mover: diagnostic 1 is free on existing baseline logs, probes train in 2h, scripted retreat is trivial, eval is the already-reproduced LIBERO-Long - watch the horizon-budget confound (retries consume timesteps) and probe false-positives, but the retry arithmetic is real.

Inherits S1's constant-metadata identifiability trap for its nuisance encoder, then bets a filter-choice contribution on the mildest photometric slice - the two-rate-vs-EMA ablation is its own kill switch.

KRR solve plus variance gate is a fast offline build with rollout-free diagnostics, but the few-shot protocol must be built from scratch and the headline already concedes LoRA may win nominal SR - a well-scoped ablation study, not a mechanism paper.

Two-stage system carrying S1's broken identifiability premise into S3's conceded-known binding: double build cost, double premise risk, and a stage-attribution ablation burden - the worst engineering bet in the batch.

Prototype bank and Hopfield layer are a few days' work, but training needs clean-vs-perturbed pairs (re-render pipeline again) and snap-to-prototype silently taxes nominal SR and novel objects - the gate-E 1-2 axis ceiling is what the build would confirm.

Needs a whole new 10-20M habit head trained plus a bandit-trained arbitration signal that's easy to get subtly wrong (reliability of what, measured how?) - real training runs and confound surface for a mechanism robots have shipped three times since 2012.
The beta rate-distortion sweep is the hidden cost: each beta is a ~20h expert finetune, times seeds, on a shared A100 - a multi-week GPU bill for a DRIBO/VDB transfer a PC calls incremental.

Ten parameters and an afternoon to code, but the error signal it filters is unobservable at deployment - you can build the wrapper, you just can't feed it; degenerates to an EMA with neuroscience branding.

A day's work and a genuine backbone-call-skipping latency win, but VLA-Corrector already published the identical event-triggered pattern (audit 0.25) and the prescribed-performance guarantee is hollow under a control reviewer.

Known recipe, one forward-pass change, fits the 4h finetune budget - easy and low-confound, but it's a zero-adaptation transplant of Analog Bits whose long-horizon causal link (seed/estimation noise drives the gap) is the same unproven premise R3 tests for 2 GPU-hours.

UCM loss reweighting collapses to Calinon-style variance-weighted LfD the moment it becomes runnable, and a per-ablation action-expert retrain with no execution-time robustness mechanism is a workshop-scale training recipe, not the plug-in the project needs.

Treats viewpoint domain shift as sensor corruption; with n=2 cameras the Dempster-Shafer apparatus degenerates to a learned scalar gate and the mandatory corruption-augmentation baseline consumes the delta — killed in all three debate rounds.

The only finalist with a fully observable error signal on the -88pt factor and genuinely cheap kill tests, but reviewer2 showed the referent Delta is identically zero on the exact init-state factor it targets, and what remains reads as visual servoing with a probe head.

Internally inconsistent as specified — the nuisance subspace is unidentifiable from clean constant-metadata LIBERO data, every rescue collapses the anti-augmentation differentiator, and the residual is INLP/LEACE concept erasure plus manifold snapping.

Episode-constant amortized nuisance inference is the most elegant framing in the batch with a decisive sub-GPU-day diagnostic, but gate C's span gap (a clean-data basis contains no appearance variation to cover test perturbations) is S1's identifiability hole wearing a different coat.

Cheapest kill test in the portfolio (2 GPU-hours) and a real anytime-compute knob, but direction-wise seed-sample aggregation is an increment inside the ACT-ensembling/VOTE/BoN crowd resting on an unevidenced premise that seed noise drives a 23-46pt gap.

Verify-postcondition-then-retry is classical robotics, but it is the only finalist whose causal chain survived attack intact: retry arithmetic attacks the multiplicative long-horizon failure structure directly, the diagnostic is nearly free on existing logs, and the failure taxonomy gives an honest RA-L/TMLR floor even at moderate gains.
A filter-choice-level contribution (two-rate vs EMA, with the EMA-match named as its own kill condition) scoped to the mildest photometric slice, in self-admitted crowded test-time-adaptation space.

Kernel-ridge posterior plus variance-gated abstention is standard GP/selective-prediction machinery on a conceded MoS-VLA basis, and a headline that pre-concedes LoRA may win nominal SR reads as an efficiency study — though the few-shot axis itself is genuinely uncharted.

Inherits S1's unlearnable nuisance subspace as its load-bearing first stage, adds two-stage attribution burden, and its own fallback plan (split into two papers) concedes it is not one contribution — 'drop stage 2 and resubmit' is the predictable meta-review.

Cleanest audited novelty in the batch (attractor pattern-completion repairing a single corrupted observation is genuinely unoccupied), but it moves 1-2 axes at added latency, viewpoint is a high-rank warp attractor basins likely cannot undo, and snap-to-prototype risks novel-object regressions.

Reliability-tracked habit/goal arbitration is already implemented on robots three times over (audit floor 0.4); the velocity-field convex blend is an implementation detail, and a ~20M-param habit head plus bandit-trained arbiter is the fiddliest build here for the thinnest delta.

DRIBO/VDB bolted onto a frozen VLA connector with a beta sweep — the canonical incremental-application paper in a crowded invariant-representation literature; likely to help robustness modestly and be unpublishable at Q1/Q2 for exactly that reason.

A ten-parameter two-rate bias filter driven by an action-execution error that does not exist at deployment; once the signal collapses to a policy-vs-demo offset it is an EMA with neuroscience branding, and no committee accepts that as a standalone contribution.

Already scooped: VLA-Corrector ships the identical event-triggered adaptive-horizon pattern (audit confidence 0.25), and the one differentiating claim — a prescribed-performance guarantee — is hollow for a monitor-only funnel; the backbone-skipping latency lever is real but not a paper.

A famous diffusion trick (Analog Bits self-conditioning) transplanted with zero VLA-specific design; the sample-quality gain is plausibly real and cheap to get, but it is ablation-grade at CoRL/RA-L unless gains are dramatic, and the seed-noise-drives-long-horizon link is unproven.

top10.name: Declarative Postcondition Retry (DPR)
top10.rationale: Highest arithmetic total by ~3.3 pts and unanimous across all three lenses: sr_gain 6/6/6 (only finalist attacking the multiplicative long-horizon failure structure directly), publication_potential 4/4/5, implementation_difficulty 2/2/3. Diagnostic 1 is free (label the existing 100-rollout 49.0% baseline logs). Its only weak axis is novelty (verify-then-retry is classical robotics, gate A failed), but the failure taxonomy + retry arithmetic gives an honest measurement-plus-fix floor even at moderate gains.

top10.name: First-Glance Nuisance Recalibration (FGNR)
top10.rationale: Highest novelty in the batch (5/5/5, episode-constant amortized nuisance inference is a genuinely distinct TTA combination) with the cleanest integration (one connector hook, closed-form fit) and a decisive sub-GPU-day kill test. Ranked 2nd despite gate C's span gap — a basis fit on appearance-invariant clean features has no affirmative reason to contain test-time viewpoint displacements — because the diagnostic falsifies that premise for <1 GPU-day before any real spend.

top10.name: Kernel-Associative Fast-Binding with Calibrated Abstention
top10.rationale: Overridden above R2 (arithmetic 23.83 vs 24.17): S3's flaw is a publishability ceiling (conceded MoS-VLA basis, known GP/selective-prediction machinery, headline concedes LoRA may win nominal SR), not a mechanism failure. It is coherent, cheap (offline matrix-solve diagnostics, no rollouts to falsify), and the only finalist on the genuinely uncharacterized few-shot axis with a distinct abstention contribution.

top10.name: Consensus-Split Decoding (CSD)
top10.rationale: Weakest novelty case in the survivor set (ACT/VOTE/BoN cluster, gate A+B+F failed) but the cheapest, most falsifiable proposal in the portfolio: a 2 GPU-hour, zero-parameter kill test whose result — the first controlled stochasticity decomposition of the 49.0% baseline — is valuable lab knowledge even on a KILL. Ranked above R2 because its premise is testable-before-build rather than internally incoherent.

top10.name: ProbeAnchor: execution-time referent-frame retargeting
top10.rationale: Demoted below S3/R3 despite the higher arithmetic: reviewer2 showed the referent Delta is identically zero under robot-init shift (its headline -88pt factor) and the full-Delta correction double-counts against a partially-perceiving closed-loop expert — a mechanism-breaking incoherence two of three rankers flagged. Retains rank 5 because the probe infrastructure (R^2=0.75, sim-state labels already in the HDF5s) is real, reusable (R4 shares it), and the replay diagnostic is near-free.

top10.name: Reconsolidation-Style Associative Memory
top10.rationale: Cleanest audited novelty among the originals (attractor pattern-completion for single-observation repair is unoccupied; novelty 5/5/6) but gate E is the honest ceiling: it affirmatively moves 1-2 axes, attractor completion cannot invert a high-rank viewpoint warp, and snap-to-prototype risks novel-object regressions. A good idea one benchmark short of a paper.

top10.name: Self-Conditioned Action Flow
top10.rationale: Overridden above C20: a proven zero-NFE-cost trick with plausible real sample-quality gains that fits the 4h finetune budget and is low-confound — but a zero-adaptation Analog Bits transplant whose long-horizon premise (per-chunk sampling noise drives the 23-46pt gap) is exactly what R3's 2 GPU-hour test would check first. Ablation-grade at Q1/Q2 unless gains are dramatic.

top10.name: Funnel-Gated Re-Inference
top10.rationale: Demoted below C26 despite higher arithmetic (inflated by latency_gain 6/5/6): novelty 1/1/1 and audit confidence 0.25 — VLA-Corrector already ships the identical event-triggered adaptive-horizon pattern, and the prescribed-performance guarantee is hollow for a monitor-only wrapper. Scooped is fatal for a publication ranking; the backbone-skip lever survives only as lab engineering.

top10.name: Reliability-Weighted Habit/Goal Blending
top10.rationale: Audit floor 0.4 — reliability-arbitrated dual control is implemented on robots three times since 2012; the surviving twist (velocity-field convex blend) is an implementation detail, a proprio-only habit branch cannot carry manipulation subtasks, and the ~20M habit head + bandit arbiter is the fiddliest build in the batch for the thinnest delta.

top10.name: RD-IB Multi-View Information Bottleneck Adapter
top10.rationale: The one candidate with genuine supporting evidence for modest robustness gains (DRIBO, VDB) — and unpublishable at Q1/Q2 for exactly that reason: a benchmark/backbone transfer of a 2017-2020 technique. Engineer lens adds the hidden cost: the beta rate-distortion sweep is ~20h of expert finetune per point per seed on a shared A100.

winner.justification: No finalist satisfies all four Phase 9 criteria simultaneously; R4 maximizes three of four and its one deficit is mitigable. Strongest expected benchmark improvement: unanimous sr_gain 6/6/6 — retry arithmetic p->p(2-p) attacks the multiplicative structure of the 23-46pt long-horizon gap at the layer where it lives, on the already-reproduced 49.0% LIBERO-Long baseline. Highest publication confidence: 4/4/5, the only candidate whose causal chain survived the full adversarial record intact (the physical-state reset answers every monitor-cluster kill: the world changes, not the query), with an honest fallback — the quantified failure taxonomy publishes even at moderate realized gains. Most realistic implementation: 2/2/3 difficulty; diagnostic 1 costs zero GPU (label existing baseline logs, pre-registered kill at <25% silent postcondition violations), probes train in 2h, scripted retreat is trivial, frozen backbone untouched. The deficit is novelty (2/3/3): verify-then-retry is classical robotics and gate A failed, so this is not the 'new mechanism' headline CoRL rewards — it publishes as a rigorous measurement-plus-mechanism paper (failure taxonomy + retry arithmetic + probe-verified recovery inside a sub-500M VLA), best targeted at RA-L or TMLR. Known risks are named and checkable: horizon-budget confound (retries consume timesteps — report matched-budget results), probe false-positive rate (<3% pre-registered), retry-independence assumption (0.5 GPU-day pilot). Runner-up R1 has the inverse profile (novelty 5/5/5 but a gate-C span gap making its premise more likely false than true); the correct portfolio move is R4 as primary with R1's cheap diagnostic run in parallel — if R1's premise survives, it becomes the novelty headline and R4 the reliable second contribution.

chair.disagreements: No axis diverged by strictly more than 3 points anywhere — the three lenses were unusually aligned, reflecting the shared debate record. Largest spreads and resolutions: (1) C13 implementation_difficulty 6 (engineer) vs 3 (reviewer/scientist ~4): the engineer priced the beta rate-distortion sweep (each beta a ~20h expert finetune, times seeds, on a shared A100) while the others scored only the small adapter; resolved toward the engineer since the sweep is intrinsic to the method's claim, reinforcing C13 at rank 10. (2) R2 robustness_gain 3/4/5: the reviewer credited the fully observable error signal on the -88pt factor, the scientist/engineer discounted for the zero-referent-Delta incoherence on that exact factor; resolved downward — the incoherence is load-bearing, hence R2's demotion from arithmetic rank 3 to rank 5. (3) R1 implementation_difficulty 5/3/4 and latency_gain 2/1/3: resolved mid — the build genuinely is one connector hook plus a closed-form fit (engineer is right), but the latency 'gain' is only amortization after a 10-frame fit, not a backbone-cost reduction. (4) S2 implementation_difficulty 6/6/4: resolved toward 6 — the reviewer under-weighted the nuisance-encoder identifiability trap S2 inherits from S1, which forces a re-render pipeline mid-build. None of these spreads changed a top-3 membership; the only ranking-relevant overrides (R2 down, C20 down, S3/C26 up) came from fatal-flaw evidence in the debate record rather than score divergence.

plans.ablation_plan:
Every ablation is a config flag in the rollout wrapper — no retrain, so all six run in the same eval sweep:

| # | Ablation | Isolates |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | No-retry frozen baseline (already have: 49.0%, seed 1000) | reference point |
| 1 | **Full DPR** (probe-gated detect + scripted retreat, budget R=2) | headline |
| 2 | **Blind retry**: retreat unconditionally every chunk boundary, no probe check | value of probe *precision* vs. raw extra-attempts budget — if this matches DPR, the probe is doing nothing and the story collapses to "retries help," which is not a contribution |
| 3 | **Oracle-postcondition retry**: same retreat primitive, gated on ground-truth MuJoCo state instead of probe readout | upper bound / cost of probe error; gap between (1) and (3) is the "probe tax" |
| 4 | **Detect-only, no recovery** (log triggers, take no action) | no-harm control — SR must equal baseline exactly; any deviation means the check itself has a side effect (timing, latency) and something is wrong with the wrapper |
| 5 | **Retry-budget sweep** R ∈ {1,2,3} | tests the p→1-(1-p)^R arithmetic empirically against real R; where it saturates or breaks tells us if independence holds |
| 6 | **FP-threshold sweep** τ (calibration curve) | shows the FP-budget choice (<3%) isn't cherry-picked; plots SR vs. episode-length overhead |
| 7 | **Few-shot × retry**: probes trained on 10/25/50 demos, crossed with retry on/off | isolates whether probe accuracy (itself demo-hungry) becomes the bottleneck at low shot |

Ablations 2 and 3 are the load-bearing ones — run those first, 1 seed each, before spending seeds on the full 3-seed table. If (2) ≈ (1), stop and report a negative result on probe precision.
plans.architecture:
DPR is a pure **inference-time wrapper**, never touches modeling_smolvla.py, the connector, or the flow-matching expert. It intercepts lerobot's rollout loop between `policy.select_action()` calls.

```
                 ┌─────────────────────────── FROZEN, UNTOUCHED ───────────────────────────┐
 camera frames → │ SmolVLM2 vision tower → connector → 32-layer text backbone → flow expert │ → action chunk
                 └─────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                                                          │ connector-output features (already computed,
                                                          │ zero extra backbone forward passes)
                                                          ▼
                              ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
                              │      DPR WRAPPER (all new, ~1.2M params)   │
                              │                                             │
                              │  1. Probe heads (2-layer MLP, reused        │
                              │     from R2's shared infra): object pose   │
                              │     regression + in-gripper classifier      │
                              │                                             │
                              │  2. Postcondition table: task_id → ordered  │
                              │     list of declarative predicates          │
                              │     (lookup, not learned — LIBERO's 10      │
                              │     instructions are fixed templates)       │
                              │                                             │
                              │  3. Chunk-boundary checker: compares        │
                              │     probe readout to pending predicate,     │
                              │     calibrated threshold τ (FP<3% budget)   │
                              │                                             │
                              │  4. Retry state machine: on trigger,        │
                              │     override the queue with a scripted      │
                              │     3-step retreat (open-loop, no model     │
                              │     call), then hand control back to the    │
                              │     frozen policy for a fresh attempt.      │
                              │     Budget: 2 retries / subgoal.            │
                              └───────────────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                            ▼
                                                  action chunk dispatched to env
```

Attachment point: `PolicyWrapper.select_action()` has the identical signature as `SmolVLAPolicy.select_action()` and is a drop-in substitute in `lerobot-eval` / `eval_shard.sh` — the eval harness doesn't need to change, only `--policy.path` points at the wrapped policy. The check fires exactly when the internal action queue empties and a fresh chunk has just been predicted (that's also the one moment the connector features for the current frame are already resident in memory, so the probe forward pass is free).

Open assumption to verify before coding (flagged, not silently assumed): SmolVLA's lerobot config exposes `chunk_size` and `n_action_steps`; if `n_action_steps < chunk_size` (partial chunk consumption + replanning), the "chunk boundary" the checker hooks is the replan boundary, not the full-chunk boundary — check `config.json` on the a100 checkpoint before wiring the hook.

plans.equations:
Postcondition check (probe-gated), at chunk boundary t for pending predicate π_k on frozen connector feature f_t:

$$\hat\pi_k(f_t) = \mathbb{1}\left[\, s\big(g_\theta(f_t),\, \pi_k^*\big) > \tau \,\right]$$

where g_θ is the 2-layer MLP probe head (object pose regression or in-gripper classifier), π_k* is the declarative target for predicate k (e.g. "object X in gripper"), s(·) is squared-error-below-margin for pose predicates or sigmoid probability for the binary in-gripper predicate, and τ is the FP-calibrated threshold (chosen so P(π̂ fires | π_k truly holds) < 0.03 on held-out demos — diagnostic 3's budget).

Idealized retry arithmetic (perfect detection, TPR=1, FPR=0), the spine of the mechanistic claim — probability of subgoal k succeeding within retry budget R:

$$P(\text{success}_k \mid R) = 1-(1-p_k)^R \quad\Rightarrow\quad R{=}2:\ \ p_k \mapsto p_k(2-p_k)$$

Realistic correction, accounting for the measured detector TPR/FPR from diagnostic 3 (this is the number that must be reported, not the idealized one):

$$
P(\text{success}_k) \approx \underbrace{p_k(1-\text{FPR})}_{\text{true success, undisturbed}} + \underbrace{p_k \cdot \text{FPR} \cdot p_k'}_{\text{true success, falsely reset, re-succeeds}} + \underbrace{(1-p_k)\cdot \text{TPR}\cdot p_k}_{\text{true failure, caught, retried, succeeds}}
$$

(the term for missed failures, (1-p_k)(1-TPR)·0, contributes nothing — that's the residual the mechanism cannot fix, and it is exactly what diagnostic 1's ≥25%-silent-violation threshold bounds).

Episode-level (task graph of K subgoals from the postcondition table, assumed independent across subgoals — an assumption, not a given, and K itself must be measured per task from the templated instruction, not assumed uniform):

$$\text{SR}_{\text{DPR}} \approx \prod_{k=1}^{K} P(\text{success}_k)$$

The empirical R=1,2,3 sweep (ablation #5) is the direct test of whether the diminishing-returns shape of $1-(1-p)^R$ actually holds in rollouts, versus retries interacting with LIBERO's fixed episode-length horizon and eating the budget instead of helping.
plans.eval_pipeline:
Harness: `lerobot-eval` / `eval_shard.sh` unchanged, `--policy.path` pointed at the DPR-wrapped policy. Suite: `libero_10` (LIBERO-Long), matching the reproduced 49.0% baseline exactly (same env config, same `--seed`).

Seeds: {1000, 2000, 3000} — 1000 reproduces the existing baseline reference point, the other two are fresh. ≥3 seeds, mean±std reported, no single-seed number presented as a result.

Primary metric: aggregate SR on LIBERO-Long, 100 rollouts/seed, vs. the 49.0% no-retry baseline (already measured — do not rerun the baseline, reuse the log).

Secondary metrics (the taxonomy deliverable, distinct from the aggregate number):
- per-subgoal success decomposition, reconstructed from postcondition-checker logs
- retry-utilization rate (fraction of episodes triggering ≥1 retry)
- realized FP rate in the field vs. the calibrated 3% target
- episode-length overhead (mean added frames/episode from retreats) and whether any episodes hit the LIBERO horizon cutoff because of it

Mandatory baselines (must beat, or report as negative result): no-retry frozen (49.0%), blind unconditional retry, oracle-postcondition retry. Per the source record's own scoping, DPR is explicitly **not** claimed to fix LIBERO-Plus init-state/viewpoint (systematic factors — that's R2's/other finalists' territory); the robustness axis here targets a named *transient/stochastic* LIBERO-Plus factor only — that factor must be picked and stated before the eval, not chosen post hoc from whichever slice looks best.

Few-shot protocol: 10/25/50-demo probe training crossed with DPR on/off, 3 seeds each, on the project's existing few-shot benchmark axis.

plans.failure_analysis:
Top 3 ways this fails, each with a cheap, pre-registered early-kill signal:

1. **Premise fails at diagnostic 1** ($0, log analysis only): if <25% of the 100 baseline failures are silent postcondition violations with ≥1 chunk of blind continuation, the mechanism has no target — most failures may instead be early, unrecoverable misperception (the frozen backbone never had the right feature) or diffuse compounding drift with no single attributable event. Kill before writing any wrapper code. Requires that the existing 49.0% baseline logs contain per-episode state, not just pass/fail; if they don't, add instrumented state logging to a rerun of a subset first (flagged compute risk above).

2. **Retry-independence assumption fails at diagnostic 2** (<0.5 GPU-day): if second-attempt success is <60% of first-attempt success, the scripted retreat is not actually returning the scene to a "fresh draw" state — e.g. a failed grasp attempt physically displaces or knocks the object, so the retry starts from a harder-than-original state, violating the i.i.d. assumption the entire p→p(2-p) arithmetic rests on. This is the single most likely failure mode given LIBERO's contact-rich manipulation.

3. **Probe FP rate blows the 3% budget in practice, task-specific** (diagnostic 3, check per-task not just pooled): some objects/poses regress worse than others (the R2 lab evidence of R²=0.75 is an aggregate, not a per-task floor), causing retry-thrashing on already-successful subgoals that eats into LIBERO's fixed episode-length horizon and can net *negative* SR on runs that would have succeeded unbothered. Must check the per-task breakdown, not just the aggregate FP number, or a bad tail task can hide inside a passing average.

Fallback if killed at (1) or (2): report as a negative result — the first controlled failure-taxonomy decomposition of a reproduced sub-500M VLA's long-horizon collapse (what fraction is silent-postcondition-violation vs. unrecoverable perception error vs. diffuse drift), which is itself a defensible measurement contribution per CLAUDE.md's "say what failed" rule, independent of whether the recovery mechanism works.

plans.theory:
Long-horizon success on LIBERO-Long is approximately the product of per-subgoal success probabilities across a task's ordered subgoal chain (pick → place → pick → place, …). A single silent failure — the policy believes a grasp succeeded and blindly continues — kills the whole episode even though the frozen policy is individually competent at each subgoal type most of the time (a 49.0% episode-level SR over an 8–13-chunk, multi-subgoal episode implies a fairly high effective per-subgoal success rate). The core theoretical move: recovery does not require a learned model of *how* to recover — it only requires (a) an observable, cheap signal that a subgoal's declared postcondition was NOT met, and (b) a scripted primitive that resets the physical scene to a demo-like approach state so the frozen policy gets a second, near-independent draw from the success distribution it was actually trained on. Nothing is predicted (no transition model, no world model — explicitly staying clear of the project's hard "no backbone gradients / no world-model" exclusions); postconditions are declarative task knowledge parsed once from LIBERO's fixed instruction templates (pick X → X-in-gripper; place X on Y → X-on-Y), not learned or forecast.

Load-bearing assumptions, each explicit and each independently falsifiable by a pre-registered diagnostic before any GPU-month is spent:
- **A1 (detectability)**: the frozen connector features carry enough state information for a cheap linear/shallow probe to read out object pose and grasp status accurately (grounded in the project's own prior evidence: ridge-probe R²=0.75 on frozen pooled features for related state-readout, methodology in `archive/scratch_pull/diag_probe.py` — demo-level train/val/test split to avoid within-demo leakage, shuffled-target control).
- **A2 (silent-failure prevalence)**: a meaningful fraction of the 49.0% baseline's failures are specifically silent postcondition violations followed by blind continuation, not early unrecoverable perception failures.
- **A3 (retry independence)**: a scripted physical retreat approximately resets the state distribution, so the second attempt's success probability is close to the first's — the retry is a fresh draw, not a harder problem.

Each assumption maps to one of the three pre-registered diagnostics; the theory is only as strong as A1–A3, and the plan is built so that a false theory is caught for single-digit GPU-hours, not a full sweep.
plans.training_pipeline:
**No policy training. No backbone/expert gradients anywhere.** The only "training" is supervised probe regression, reusing R2's already-validated infrastructure.

Data: LIBERO-Long demo HDF5s already cached in LeRobot format. Additional requirement (state explicitly, not assumed silently): per-timestep object 6-DoF pose and gripper-contact/grasp boolean from the underlying MuJoCo sim state. `archive/scratch_pull/diag_probe.py`'s existing cache (`pooled`, `actions`, `demo_id`) does not yet include these — confirm before coding whether the original LIBERO HDF5 (pre-lerobot-conversion) sim state is still reachable alongside the lerobot dataset, or whether it must be re-derived by replaying demos through robosuite (same mechanism used for the R2 lab-evidence probe). This is the plan's first concrete engineering task.

Probe architecture: 2-layer MLP, hidden width 256, input = frozen connector-output feature (SmolVLA hidden dim), reused across both probe heads (pose regression, in-gripper classification) — matches R2's already-validated architecture.

Losses: MSE on standardized (x,y,z) [+ orientation if LIBERO's object-pose state includes it, else position-only — verify against sim-state field before committing] for pose regression; binary cross-entropy for the in-gripper/grasp-contact classifier.

Hyperparameters: Adam, lr=1e-3, batch=256, ~20 epochs, weight decay 1e-4, cosine LR decay.

Split: demo-level 60/20/20 (not sample-level — adjacent timesteps within a demo are near-duplicates and a random split leaks, per the existing `diag_probe.py` convention). Val picks the regularization/early-stop point; test reports the number that gets used downstream.

Seeds: ≥3 seeds {0,1,2} for probe training (it feeds a downstream rollout metric, so probe variance must be characterized, not treated as fixed).

**Success criterion, written and pre-registered before any full-policy rollout is launched** (verbatim from the finalist record, restated here as the launch gate):
1. Failure taxonomy on the existing 100-rollout, 49.0%, seed-1000 baseline logs: PROCEED only if ≥25% of failures are silent postcondition violations with ≥1 chunk of blind continuation after the violation. ($0 GPU.)
2. Retry-independence pilot, 20 episodes with scripted retreat after a detected grasp failure: PROCEED only if second-attempt per-grasp success ≥60% of first-attempt rate. (<0.5 GPU-day.)
3. False-positive budget: probe-verifier false-alarm rate on successful subgoals must be <3%, checked per-task not just pooled. (folded into probe held-out eval, ~0 extra GPU.)

Only if all three pass does the full wrapper get built and the eval sweep launched.

plans.theory:
**Assumption 1** (from LIBERO-Plus 2510.13626, cited not re-derived): appearance perturbations (camera pose, lighting, background, distractor) are sampled once per episode and held fixed for its duration — licenses episode-level, not per-frame, nuisance estimation.

**Assumption 2** (UNVALIDATED — this is exactly what killed gate C and what Phase 0 exists to test): the displacement these perturbations induce in frozen SmolVLM2 connector-feature space is approximately low-rank (K<=32) and linearly separable from task-content directions.

**Assumption 3** (lab evidence, cited): linear-probe R²=0.75 recovering object/gripper state from frozen features — motivates "repair the conditioning" over "relearn the policy," but does not by itself establish Assumption 2.

**GATE-C AMENDMENT — stated explicitly, not picked silently.** R1's own gate result (`C_mechanism: false`) identified a real analytical gap: vanilla LIBERO renders each task with a *fixed* camera pose and lighting config across all clean training demos, so a basis fit purely from between-episode variation on clean data has ~zero signal in the camera/lighting directions and is expected to be content-contaminated. R1's spec also insists on "no corruption generator, clean-data-only training" to avoid collapsing into the augmentation baseline that killed C7/S1/S2. These two commitments are mutually exclusive — an identifiable nuisance basis and zero exposure to nuisance variation cannot both hold. Two readings, named explicitly:

- **Path A (adopted amendment)**: offline, re-render a small stratified sample (~2-5k frames) of *already-cached MuJoCo states* from the existing demo HDF5 at K_render=6-8 synthetic camera-pose/lighting offsets spanning LIBERO-Plus's own documented factor ranges. Extract frozen connector features via forward pass only (no new trajectories, no new action labels, no expert gradient). Seed B directly from paired canonical-vs-offset feature differences (self-supervised SVD, no action-loss anywhere). This is distinct in kind from the augmentation baseline (which trains the *policy's action loss* on corrupted pixels) — it only identifies a geometric direction in a frozen feature space.
- **Path B (literal original spec, kept as a control)**: between-episode PCA on unperturbed clean features only. Run it anyway, expected to fail — this is the cheap empirical falsification of gate C's concern that the project's own diagnostic discipline demands ("run the cheap diagnostic first").

The plan below implements Path A as primary, Path B as a mandatory negative-result control arm.
plans.equations:
Let f_t ∈ R^{N×d} be per-frame connector-output token features; f̄_task = mean over clean-train features for a given task (task-conditioned centering).

Path B (control, expected to fail): r_i = f̄_{episode_i} − f̄_{task(i)}; B_unsup = top-K eigenvectors of Cov({r_i}).

Path A (seeded basis): for cached MuJoCo state s and synthetic offset j (camera/light), Δ_j(s) = f(s, cam_j) − f(s, cam_0). Stack ΔM = [Δ_1; Δ_2; …] over sampled states/offsets; B_seed = top-K left singular vectors of SVD(ΔM).

Purity filter: keep column b_k of B iff |probe(f) − probe(f − α·b_k)| / perturbation_range < 0.05 for α spanning the observed offset magnitude, where probe(·) is the frozen R2/S1-style state-readout MLP (object pose / gripper state). This enforces that nuisance directions carry no task-content signal.

Energy model (quadratic case, Mahalanobis under clean-feature statistics μ, Σ): E_φ(f) = (f−μ)ᵀ Σ⁻¹ (f−μ), extendable to a K-component GMM: E_φ(f) = −log Σ_k π_k N(f; μ_k, Σ_k).

Online coefficient fit over the first W=10-frame pooled feature f̄_W = (1/W)Σ_{t=1}^{W} f_t:
ĉ = argmin_c E_φ(f̄_W − B c)
Closed form for the quadratic case: ĉ = (BᵀΣ⁻¹B)⁻¹ BᵀΣ⁻¹(f̄_W − μ).

No-harm gate: apply correction iff E_φ(f̄_W − Bĉ) < E_φ(f̄_W) − τ, else ĉ=0 (identity). τ calibrated on a clean-episode holdout so the false-trigger rate is ≤5%.

Two-rate refinement across the episode (t > W, fresh windowed estimate c_t every ~50 steps):
c_slow ← c_slow + η_slow (c_t − c_slow),  c_fast ← c_fast + η_fast (c_t − c_fast),  η_fast ≫ η_slow.
Applied correction uses c_slow (this is the direct C19-preemption target, tested against a single-EMA ablation).

Final repaired token: f_t' = f_t − B·c_slow(t).

**1. Identifiability failure (the gate-C risk, highest-probability failure mode).** Even with Path A re-rendering, the induced feature displacement may not be low-rank or may be entangled with content (a large-angle viewpoint change permutes token-to-object correspondence rather than translating along a linear direction; this is structurally different from a small lighting/color shift). Early kill signal: Phase 0 step 0d, probe-R² recovery <40% on held-out viewpoint or lighting — cost ~1-2 GPU-days to learn this, before any rollout is run. Fallback framing: report as a negative/measurement result — "frozen SmolVLA connector-feature displacement under LIBERO-Plus appearance shift is [not] low-rank/content-separable," which is itself informative to the field about the ceiling on repair-based (vs. retrain-based) robustness fixes at this representation layer.

**2. Fair-baseline dominance.** The corruption-augmented adapter, trained with real action supervision on the identical re-rendered frames, matches or beats FGNR's SR — this exact failure killed C7 (R1/R2/R3), S1 (all three rounds), and S2 (gate E). Early kill signal: diagnostic (2). Fallback framing: if SR is merely comparable (not worse, not better), FGNR's residual claim narrows to the *data-efficiency/compute* axes (zero-shot, zero gradient steps, ~zero marginal FLOPs after warm-up) rather than a raw-SR win — report honestly as "comparable robustness at a different, favorable point on the compute/supervision tradeoff," not as a SR victory it didn't achieve.

**3. Gate/threshold brittleness.** τ mis-calibrated: either the gate never fires (module ships as a no-op, zero measured effect anywhere) or it over-triggers on in-distribution nominal episodes, silently costing the 49.0% no-harm floor. Early kill signal: diagnostic (3), >1pt SR drop on the nominal protocol. Fallback: widen τ and re-run diagnostic (3) once (not an unlimited hyperparameter search — one re-calibration pass, then accept or kill).

**Overall recommendation embedded in the plan**: Phase 0 is a strict, cheap (~1-2 GPU-day) gate. Given R1's own gate result (`C_mechanism: false`, 5/6 gates, zero debate rounds run) and that this batch's four fully-debated siblings (C4, C7, R2, S1) were all killed on structurally similar grounds (premise identifiability, fair-baseline dominance, one-axis-not-three), the honest prior on R1 clearing Phase 0 AND beating the fair baseline is LOW. **Attachment point**: post-hoc wrapper around `SmolVLAPolicy.select_action()` in lerobot 0.4.4. No change to `modeling_smolvla.py` internals; backbone (SigLIP+SmolLM2) and flow-matching action expert stay frozen and untouched. New code lives in a sibling module (e.g. `lerobot/policies/smolvla/krr_wrapper.py`) that calls the existing policy twice-ish per decision: once to get the pooled content feature (already computed internally for expert conditioning — just add a hook to return it) and once to get the zero-shot chunk.

```
 obs_t, lang ──► [FROZEN SmolVLA: SigLIP + SmolLM2 + connector] ──► prefix features
                          │                                              │
                          │ (hook: mean-pool prefix tokens → f_t ∈ R^d_f)│
                          ▼                                              ▼
                 [FROZEN flow-matching expert]                    content feature f_t
                          │
                          ▼
                 a_base ∈ R^{chunk_size×act_dim}   (deterministic: average over
                                                     K_ode=8 fixed-noise ODE draws)
                          │
        ┌─────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐
        │        NEW: KRR-Bind wrapper (no grad)      │
        │  1. c_base = B^T (a_base - μ)                │
        │  2. k* = [k(f_t, f_i)]_{i=1..N}  (N=demo pts)│
        │  3. Δĉ = k*^T α           (matrix-vector, ms)│
        │  4. σ² = k(f_t,f_t) − k*^T(K+λI)^{-1}k*      │
        │  5. gate: g = 1[σ² ≤ τ]                      │
        │  6. c_final = c_base + g·Δĉ                  │
        │  7. a_final = μ + B c_final                  │
        └─────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                          ▼
                 action chunk sent to env
```

`B` (D×K PCA basis, D=chunk_size·act_dim, K≈64), `μ` (mean chunk), and the meta-hyperparameters (kernel length-scale ℓ, signal variance σ_f², ridge λ, abstention threshold τ) are fit **once, offline**, on a calibration task set disjoint from the final eval tasks, and then frozen. Per new few-shot task, only `{f_i, Δc_i}_{i=1..N}` (the support set) and `α = (K_NN+λI)^{-1}ΔC` (one matrix solve, N≤~250×250) are computed — no gradient steps, no new persistent weights per task. This is exactly the "matrix solve replaces fine-tuning" claim in the S3 spec; the wrapper degrades to identity (pure zero-shot SmolVLA) whenever the gate abstains.

Generalizes to any EE-chunk VLA (pi0, OFT) by swapping `a_base` source and the pooled-feature hook; the wrapper does not depend on flow-matching specifics beyond needing *some* deterministic base-chunk estimate.
plans.theory:
**Claim.** A frozen VLA's flow-matching action expert already encodes most of the task-relevant action manifold; residual few-shot task specialization is well-approximated by a *low-rank, smooth* correction over a shared schema basis, and how far a query is from the small demo support set is knowable from kernel distance in content-feature space — giving a free, principled confidence signal that a gradient-based few-shot adapter (LoRA) does not provide.

**Assumptions made explicit (this is the load-bearing, falsifiable part):**
1. *Shared-basis assumption*: LIBERO-Long action-chunk residuals-across-tasks live near a K≈64-dim linear subspace, so a task-specific correction is well captured by ~64 coefficients rather than needing full-rank fine-tuning. **Unverified — this is exactly the premise the gate audit flagged as "conceded prior art, not novel" (MoS-VLA already does this for a *single* demo's coefficients).** S3's own delta is not this assumption but the next two.
2. *Content-feature locality assumption*: the frozen VLM's pooled prefix feature is a meaningful metric space in which "near a demo" ⇒ "policy behaves like the demo's local correction," and "far from all demos" ⇒ correction is untrustworthy. This is the standard kernel-ridge/GP smoothness assumption; it can fail if the pooled feature discards exactly the geometry that matters (a real risk — SmolVLA's pooling was never trained for this).
3. *Deterministic base chunk exists*: `a_base` (zero-shot, no demos) is a stable enough reference that a residual `Δa = a_demo − a_base` is a coherent regression target rather than noise dominated by flow-matching sampling variance. Mitigated by averaging over K_ode=8 fixed-seed ODE integrations, but not proven low-variance for LIBERO-Long's longer/harder tasks.
4. *Honest caveat carried from the gate result*: Gate A (novelty) and Gate F (publication) both failed in the committee record (`gate_pass_count=4/6`, no debate round was even run) — the residual mechanism (GP/kernel-ridge posterior + variance-gated abstention) maps closely to known selective-prediction/uncertainty-gating machinery (ThriftyDAgger-style) once the basis is conceded as non-novel. This plan proceeds as instructed, but the diagnostics below are deliberately the cheapest possible falsifiers of assumptions 1–3, run *before* any rollout compute, so a likely negative result is caught for ~1 GPU-day, not a GPU-month.
plans.equations:
PCA basis (offline, over training chunks $\{a_i\in\mathbb R^D\}$, $D=\text{chunk\_size}\times\text{act\_dim}$):
$$\mu=\tfrac1M\sum_i a_i,\quad \tilde A = [a_i-\mu],\quad \tilde A = U\Sigma V^\top,\quad B = V_{:,1:K}\in\mathbb R^{D\times K}$$
$$c_i = B^\top(a_i-\mu)\in\mathbb R^K \qquad \hat a_i = \mu + Bc_i$$

Per-demo residual target (content feature $f_t$ = mean-pooled frozen prefix tokens at time $t$):
$$\Delta a_t = a_t^{\text{demo}} - a_t^{\text{base}},\qquad \Delta c_t = B^\top \Delta a_t$$

Kernel (RBF on pooled content feature, hyperparameters $\ell,\sigma_f^2$ calibrated offline):
$$k(f,f') = \sigma_f^2\exp\!\Big(-\frac{\|f-f'\|^2}{2\ell^2}\Big)$$

Closed-form multi-output kernel ridge over the $N$ support points $\{(f_i,\Delta c_i)\}_{i=1}^N$:
$$K_{NN}\in\mathbb R^{N\times N},\ [K_{NN}]_{ij}=k(f_i,f_j),\qquad \alpha = (K_{NN}+\lambda I)^{-1}\Delta C,\ \ \Delta C\in\mathbb R^{N\times K}$$

Query-time prediction (standard GP posterior mean/variance):
$$k_*(f)=[k(f,f_1),\dots,k(f,f_N)]^\top,\qquad \Delta\hat c(f) = k_*(f)^\top\alpha$$
$$\sigma^2(f) = k(f,f) - k_*(f)^\top (K_{NN}+\lambda I)^{-1}k_*(f)$$

Abstention gate and final action ($\tau$ calibrated offline, e.g. 90th percentile of in-support $\sigma^2$):
$$g(f)=\mathbb 1[\sigma^2(f)\le\tau],\qquad a_{\text{final}}(f) = a_{\text{base}}(f) + g(f)\cdot B\,\Delta\hat c(f)$$

Success-criterion statistics (pre-registered, see training/eval pipeline):
$$\text{Reconstruction ratio} = \frac{\text{L2}_{\text{KRR, held-out demo}}}{\text{L2}_{\text{LoRA, held-out demo}}} \le 1.5 \ \Rightarrow\ \text{pass diagnostic (i)}$$
$$\text{Spearman}\big(\sigma^2(f),\ \|a_{\text{pred}}(f)-a_{\text{true}}(f)\|_2\big) \ge 0.3 \ \Rightarrow\ \text{pass diagnostic (ii)}$$
plans.training_pipeline:
**No backbone/expert gradients anywhere.** Three offline stages, all CPU/matrix-solve-cheap except the forward-pass caching.

*Stage 0 — basis + meta-calibration (once, before any task-specific work):*
- Data: ~50–100 demos sampled across the full LIBERO-Long training suite (10 tasks), held out from the tasks used in Phase-1/2 eval so calibration hyperparameters aren't fit on test tasks.
- Compute: one frozen forward pass per frame (SigLIP+SmolLM2+connector) to get $f_t$, plus one zero-shot flow decode per chunk-anchor timestep (K_ode=8 fixed-seed Euler integrations, averaged) to get $a_t^{\text{base}}$. Cache both to disk (features are ~1KB/frame; trivial storage).
- Fit $B,\mu$ via SVD on all cached $(a^{\text{demo}}-a^{\text{base}})$ pairs pooled across the calibration tasks (K=64 components; sweep K∈{16,32,64,128} and pick by held-out reconstruction L2, report the curve — this IS the "shared-basis assumption" test, done once, cheaply).
- Calibrate $\ell,\sigma_f^2,\lambda$ by 5-fold CV over calibration-task support sets, minimizing held-out $\Delta c$ prediction error.
- Calibrate $\tau$ as the 90th percentile of in-support $\sigma^2$ pooled across calibration tasks (controls false-abstain rate on nominal, in-distribution queries to ≤10%).
- **Success criterion, written before Stage 0 runs:** reconstruction-error curve must show K=64 within 20% of K=128 (basis saturates — if it doesn't, the shared-basis premise is already shaky and K must be reported honestly, not silently inflated).

*Stage 1 — pre-registered kill diagnostic (per S3 spec, <1 GPU-day, offline, no rollouts):*
- (i) Shared-basis viability: on 3 held-out calibration tasks, leave-one-demo-out CV — compare closed-form KRR chunk reconstruction L2 vs. a LoRA fine-tune (rank 8, on the action-expert only, same k=10 demos, 200 steps, lr swept {1e-4,3e-4,1e-3}) on the same held-out demo. **Kill S3 if KRR L2 > 1.5× LoRA L2**, averaged over 3 seeds (demo subsample seed).
- (ii) Abstention calibration: on held-out states from the same calibration tasks plus LIBERO-Plus init-state-perturbed rollouts of those tasks (as an OOD probe), compute Spearman correlation between $\sigma^2(f)$ and true chunk L2 error against logged expert actions. **Kill the abstention axis if Spearman < 0.3** (fall back to reporting KRR-binding-only, no third dimension — mirrors R2's own pre-authorized ILC drop clause).
- Both diagnostics run on cached features from Stage 0 plus one extra small forward pass for the OOD probe set — no policy rollouts required to falsify.

*Stage 2 — per-task few-shot fit (only if Stage 1 passes; this is the "training" the eval pipeline actually exercises):*
- For each eval task × demo-count k∈{10,25,50} × seed∈{0,1,2} (≥3 seeds, seed controls which k demos are subsampled from the task's full demo set): cache $(f_i,\Delta c_i)$ for each support point (one chunk-anchor per non-overlapping `n_action_steps` window per demo, ~5–15 points/demo depending on task length), solve $\alpha=(K_{NN}+\lambda I)^{-1}\Delta C$ (closed form, seconds, N≤~750).
- LoRA baseline trained the same way at every (task,k,seed) cell for fair comparison: rank 8 adapter on the flow-matching expert's linear layers, 200 steps, best of the 3 swept LRs from Stage 1, same demo subsample.
plans.eval_pipeline:
**Benchmarks:** LIBERO-Long few-shot protocol (10/25/50-demo adaptation), the explicitly-uncharacterized axis named in the mission brief. Reduced-scope pilot first (5 of the 10 LIBERO-Long tasks, chosen to span short/long-horizon and single/multi-object variants), full 10-task sweep only if the pilot clears its success bar.

**Methods compared (4):** (a) zero-shot SmolVLA (no adaptation, the 49.0% baseline's own policy — 0 demos used), (b) LoRA few-shot fine-tune (gradient baseline, rank 8, per Stage 1 recipe), (c) S3 full (KRR-bind + abstention gate), (d) S3-no-gate ablation (KRR-bind, correction always applied, gate disabled — isolates the abstention axis's contribution).

**Rollout counts / seeds:** Pilot: 5 tasks × {10,25,50} demos × 3 seeds × 10 rollouts/task/config × 4 methods = 1,800 rollouts. Full (only if pilot passes): 10 tasks × 3 demo-counts × 3 seeds × 10 rollouts × 4 methods = 3,600 rollouts, reported mean±std over the 3 seeds. Eval rollout seed follows the reproduced-baseline convention (seed 1000 family, offset per replicate) — never fewer than 3 seeds per the project's non-negotiable rule.

**Metrics:**
- Success rate (SR) per (task, demo-count, method) — primary.
- Confident-wrong rate: fraction of *failed* rollouts where the gate did NOT abstain (i.e., high-confidence wrong action) — this is S3's distinct 3rd axis, measured as failure-mode composition, not SR.
- Params added (trained weights, not counting the frozen basis) and wall-clock adaptation time per task (KRR: matrix solve, seconds; LoRA: ~200 steps, minutes) — reported as the parameter/gradient-efficiency axis.
- Inference latency overhead (extra wrapper compute per `select_action` call — should be sub-millisecond: one N×N matrix-vector product, N≤~750).

**Baselines beyond LoRA:** zero-shot is the honest floor; no full backbone-unfreeze baseline (excluded by CLAUDE.md's hard frozen-backbone constraint).

plans.ablation_plan:
Isolate each of S3's three claimed axes with one component removed at a time, holding everything else fixed:

1. **Basis-only vs. content-conditioned correction**: replace $\Delta\hat c(f)$ with the *unconditional* mean of $\{\Delta c_i\}$ (task-average correction, no kernel regression) — tests whether the kernel-conditioning on content features adds anything over a flat task-level shift. If flat-shift matches KRR SR, the "content-feature locality" claim (theory assumption 2) is empty.
2. **KRR vs. LoRA** (already the primary Stage-1/2 baseline): isolates whether closed-form binding matches gradient adaptation on nominal SR — this is the headline efficiency-vs-SR tradeoff the paper must report honestly, including if LoRA wins.
3. **Gate on vs. off** (S3-full vs. S3-no-gate, already in the 4-method eval matrix): isolates the abstention axis specifically — the paper's 3rd claimed dimension lives entirely in this ablation's confident-wrong-rate delta.
4. **Basis rank K sweep** {16,32,64,128}: isolates how much of any gain is "more capacity" vs. "the right correction," and directly reports the shared-basis saturation curve promised in Stage 0.
5. **Kernel bandwidth ablation** (isotropic RBF vs. a trivial 1-NN lookup, i.e. $\ell\to0$): tests whether the GP smoothness assumption buys anything over nearest-neighbor retrieval — a reviewer's most likely "this reduces to VINN" attack, so pre-empt it directly.
plans.failure_analysis:
**Top 3 failure modes, each with an early, cheap kill signal already built into Stage 1:**

1. **Shared-basis premise is false for LIBERO-Long** (residuals are not low-rank/linear across tasks — plausible given LIBERO-Long's diverse long-horizon subtask structure vs. the simpler settings where MoS-VLA-style bases were validated). *Kill signal:* Stage-1 diagnostic (i), KRR reconstruction L2 > 1.5× LoRA on held-out demos. *Fallback:* report as a negative result — "closed-form low-rank binding does not match gradient adaptation on LIBERO-Long's action-residual structure," with the reconstruction-error curve as the evidence, and stop before any rollout spend.

2. **Posterior variance doesn't track real error** (pooled content feature discards exactly the geometry that determines whether a correction is trustworthy — a real risk since SmolVLA's pooling was never trained for this purpose). *Kill signal:* Stage-1 diagnostic (ii), Spearman < 0.3. *Fallback:* drop the abstention axis, ship KRR-bind alone as a 2-axis (data-efficiency, parameter-efficiency) contribution — explicitly weaker, and per the gate record this alone likely still fails novelty (Gate A already flagged the basis as conceded prior art), so this fallback should trigger an honest stop-and-report rather than continuing to a full sweep.

3. **Novelty/publication risk materializes as designed-for in the gate record** (Gate A_novelty=false, Gate F_publication=false, `gate_pass_count=4/6`, no debate round ever run for S3 — this candidate did not clear the same bar C4/C7/R2/S1 cleared before being killed in debate). Even a clean empirical win reduces, per the gate's own reasoning, to "selective-prediction/GP-posterior gating bolted onto a conceded-non-novel basis" — a reviewer maps it to ThriftyDAgger-style uncertainty gating plus VINN-style nonparametric retrieval. *Early signal:* none of the diagnostics can catch this — it is a novelty-positioning risk, not an empirical one. *Fallback framing:* if Stage 1 passes and Phase-1 pilot shows real gains, position the paper honestly as a measurement/efficiency study ("frozen-VLA few-shot adaptation is achievable at zero gradient steps with comparable SR and a novel confident-wrong-rate reduction") rather than claiming a new mechanism — RA-L short or workshop-appropriate, not a CoRL headline, consistent with the committee's own R3 assessment of this cluster.
plans.params_added: Frozen basis $B,\mu$: $D\times K \approx 350\times64 \approx 22{,}400$ floats (fit via SVD, not gradient-trained). Meta-calibration parameters (fit once offline, shared across all tasks): kernel length-scale $\ell$, signal variance $\sigma_f^2$, ridge $\lambda$, abstention threshold $\tau$ — 4 scalars (or up to $d_f$+3 if ARD length-scales are used per content-feature dimension, ~1K params). Per-task support set $\{f_i,\Delta c_i\}$ and $\alpha$ are *not* persistent trained weights — they are recomputed per task via a closed-form solve and can be discarded after inference (analogous to a KNN index, not a model checkpoint). **Total genuinely learned/calibrated parameters: ~1K, zero per-task trained weights**, vs. LoRA's rank-8 adapter (~hundreds of K params *per task*, persisted).
